An Exact Poisson Mixture Representation of Siler Remaining Life Expectancy
summary: The Siler model describes mortality from birth to old age as the sum of a declining immaturity hazard, a constant background hazard, and an increasing senescence hazard. No standard closed form is available for its remaining life expectancy, which must therefore be evaluated by numerical integration. We show that Siler remaining life expectancy at age $x$ is a Poisson mixture of Gompertz-Makeham remaining life expectancies, that is, a Poisson-weighted average of life expectancies in models with only a constant background hazard and an exponentially increasing senescence hazard. All components share the senescence hazard. Their background hazards increase from one component to the next by the rate at which immaturity mortality declines. The Poisson mean is the immaturity hazard that remains to be accumulated after age $x$. This representation yields an exact series of generalized exponential integrals with a closed-form bound on the truncation error. Replacing the background hazard by its discounted counterpart also gives the Laplace transform of the remaining lifetime. The mixture bounds the life expectancy lost to immaturity mortality: up to a term below the reciprocal of $a_2+b_1$, this loss equals the probability of an immaturity death times the life expectancy with the immaturity hazard removed. In annual Siler fits to Swedish female mortality, we estimate that the loss at birth fell from 4.3 years in 1900 to less than 0.01 years in 2020, which accounts for 15% of the gain in life expectancy at birth over the period.

IER3-N-cadherin axis contributes to apoptosis resistance in dermal fibroblasts under profibrotic conditions
summary: Background: Persistent activation and resistance to apoptosis of dermal fibroblasts contribute to pathological skin fibrosis. Immediate early response 3 (IER3) is a stress-responsive protein involved in cell survival, but its role in cutaneous fibrosis remains unclear. We investigated the functional significance of IER3 in dermal fibroblasts and its potential contribution to fibrosis. Methods: IER3 expression was examined in skin samples from patients with systemic sclerosis, keloids, and hypertrophic scars. Primary human dermal fibroblasts were stimulated with transforming growth factor-{beta}1 (TGF-{beta}1). RNA sequencing, siRNA-mediated gene silencing, quantitative PCR, and flow cytometric apoptosis assays were performed to investigate the downstream mechanisms and functional consequences of IER3 expression. Results: IER3 expression was increased in dermal fibroblasts within fibrotic skin lesions and was induced by TGF-{beta}1 independently of SMAD3 and MEK/ERK signaling. Transcriptomic analysis identified CDH2, encoding N-cadherin, as a downstream target of IER3. Moreover, TGF-{beta}1 induced CDH2 expression in a SMAD3 phosphorylation-dependent manner. IER3 knockdown attenuated TGF-{beta}1-induced CDH2 expression, whereas CDH2 knockdown did not affect IER3 expression. Furthermore, CDH2 knockdown enhanced staurosporine-induced apoptosis in TGF-{beta}1-stimulated fibroblasts, accompanied by a shift in apoptosis-related gene expression toward a pro-apoptotic profile. Conclusion: Our findings identify a previously unrecognized IER3-N-cadherin regulatory axis that may promote dermal fibroblast survival by suppressing apoptosis under profibrotic conditions. Targeting this pathway may represent a novel therapeutic strategy for persistent skin fibrosis.

title: Lac1-dependent ceramide synthesis couples septum assembly to cell separation in Schizosaccharomyces pombe
summary: Ceramides are precursors of complex sphingolipids and bioactive membrane lipids. In the fission yeast Schizosaccharomyces pombe, they are produced by a ceramide synthase with two catalytic subunits, Lac1 and Lag1, which are redundant but not functionally equivalent: only Lac1 is required for normal growth and cell size. Why Lac1 has this unique role, and how ceramide synthesis contributes to cell morphogenesis, remain unknown. Here, we show that Lac1 couples septum assembly to cell separation. Cells lacking Lac1 die predominantly during cell separation and build septa with a thinner primary layer and markedly thicker secondary layers, accompanied by altered deposition of {beta}-(1,3)-glucans and galactomannan. These defects are not rescued by osmotic stabilization. The essential glucan synthase Bgs4 is mislocalized to cytoplasmic granules, and total {beta}-(1,3)-glucan synthase activity is partially reduced. Nevertheless, Ags1, Bgs1 and Bgs4 accumulate to higher levels and persist almost twice as long at the division site, indicating defective clearance rather than delivery of the septum-synthesis machinery. Plasma membrane sterol distribution remains unaffected. To accurately impair ceramide synthesis, we isolated thermosensitive lac1-ts alleles in a lag1{Delta} background. Their substitutions cluster in the conserved TRAM/LAG1 domain. Metabolic labeling showed that these alleles reduce ceramide synthesis at the restrictive temperature. Molecular dynamics simulations indicated that two substitutions perturb distinct contacts with C26-CoA, while Lac1-M167T loses its endoplasmic reticulum localization. Acute inactivation recapitulates the deletion phenotype, causing septum accumulation and cell death. Together, our findings establish that Lac1-dependent ceramide synthesis is required for the orderly completion of septum assembly and cell separation.

title: Polycomb Marked Promoter Methylation Gains in Aging and Cancer are Independent of Replication
summary: DNA methylation alterations are hallmark features of aging and cancer, occurring early during tumor initiation. Yet how these changes evolve during early tumorigenesis, and whether oncogenic signaling actively drives them, remains poorly understood due to limitations in resolving this at the longitudinal and clonal level. Here we developed a genome-wide DNA methylation profiling method for low DNA amounts and applied it to single stem cell-derived clones from a BRAFV600E -inducible mouse colon organoid model, tracking nucleotide-level methylation heterogeneity over time. BRAFV600E induction produced stepwise methylation divergence consistent with progressive clonal takeover, in contrast to gradual epigenetic drift in uninduced controls. Strikingly, while the specific CpG sites altered differed between BRAFV600E and control lineages, they converged on the same genomic elements. Particularly, Polycomb-marked promoter CpG-island methylation gains were not induced or accelerated by BRAFV600E, challenging models in which oncogenic signaling or cell proliferation actively instructs de novo methylation of Polycomb-targeted promoters. Instead, these gains tracked with "biological aging" independent of replication, which was validated across independent aging, cancer, and cell-line datasets. BRAFV600E -induced clones additionally showed progressive loss of intestinal lineage-specification transcription factor programs, consistent with selection for cells adapted to oncogenic stress. Together, these findings show that epigenetic trajectories during early tumor development, are rooted in baseline, age-dependent drivers of epigenetic alterations, and that oncogenic signaling acts primarily by selecting and expanding clones bearing pre-existing, age-associated epigenetic drift rather than instructing new methylation. Our findings have implications for how promoter methylation is interpreted as a cancer biomarker and for identifying upstream aging-associated processes as targets for early intervention.

title: Wolffia globosa -derived nanovesicles as a natural source of bioactive metabolites with neuroprotective potential against methylglyoxal-induced oxidative stress
summary: Plant-derived nanovesicles (PDNVs) have attracted increasing attention for their potential biomedical applications, particularly in oxidative stress-related diseases and neuroprotection. Wolffia globosa, an emerging functional food and potential future food source, is rich in phytochemicals associated with health-promoting properties. Harnessing W. globosa-derived nanovesicles (WGNVs) represents a promising strategy for expanding the biomedical applications of this plant. In this study, WGNVs were isolated and characterized, and their neuroprotective potential was evaluated in vitro. The isolated WGNVs exhibited nanoscale dimensions and a lipid bilayer structure. Biochemical analyses revealed substantial total phenolic and flavonoid contents, alongside intrinsic antioxidant activities. Untargeted metabolomic profiling identified a diverse repertoire of metabolites, including major constituents subsequently validated using independent analytical approaches. These findings provided a foundation for investigating the neuroprotective effects of WGNVs in a methylglyoxal (MGX)-induced model of neuronal oxidative stress. High-resolution confocal microscopy demonstrated the cellular localization of WGNVs within neuronal cells, providing evidence of interactions between plant-derived nanovesicles and neuronal cells. WGNV treatment attenuated MGX-induced free radical accumulation and oxidative stress responses while preserving cellular morphology integrity. Collectively, this study provides foundational evidence of the physicochemical characteristics, metabolite composition, and in vitro neuroprotective potential of WGNVs. These findings highlight WGNVs as a promising naturally derived nanocarrier platform for investigating plant-animal interkingdom interactions and exploring potential therapeutic applications across a broad range of biomedical fields.

title: Integrated metabolomics and proteomics from voxelated cortical hemispheres of adult rhesus monkeys
summary: The spatial organization of molecular networks across cortex likely contributes to differences in local circuit vulnerability in aging and Alzheimer's disease; yet many existing molecular datasets sacrifice spatial structure, sampling only a handful of regions per brain. Here, we present a framework for generating spatially registered, paired metabolomic and proteomic maps across an entire cortical hemisphere of an adult rhesus monkey, at millimeter resolution. One hemisphere each from two animals was harvested under controlled conditions, approximately flattened, and hand dissected at different sampling resolutions (roughly 2.5 and 4 mm/side) into tissue voxels. Each voxel was split after homogenization and extraction to provide matched aliquots for targeted metabolomics and deep untargeted proteomics. To handle these high dimensional data, we developed PChclust, a principal component guided feature clustering algorithm. For cross omic integration, we developed a spatially regularized sparse canonical correlation analysis (sr-sCCA), which incorporates spatial neighborhood structure via graph Laplacian smoothing. We recover meaningful biology: Molecular similarity between neighboring voxels decayed with distance in both modalities, confirming that voxelation captures spatially organized biological variance. The sr-sCCA identified joint proteome-metabolome components with coherent cortical gradients that were conserved across animals. Pathway enrichment analysis recovered brain relevant ontologies and reconstructed complete metabolic circuits from single voxels.

title: A Reproducible Pre-Transplant γδ T-cell Effector Signature Reveals Immune-Metabolic Programs Associated with Kidney Allograft Rejection
summary: Despite optimized immunosuppression, acute kidney transplant rejection affects 10-20% of recipients within the first year, and no reliable pre-transplant molecular test exists to identify patients at high risk, independent of the donor HLA matching. Across three independent cohorts of kidney transplant recipients, profiled by bulk RNA-sequencing with T-cell receptor repertoire analysis, flow cytometry, CyTOF with paired metabolomics, we identified a reproducible depletion of {gamma}{delta} T cells associated with rejection: an elevated {beta}/{gamma}{delta} T cell ratio in two post-transplant, biopsy-matched cohorts, and depletion of specific {gamma}{delta} T effector clusters in a third, longitudinally sampled cohort. In this third cohort, {gamma}{delta} T cell depletion was already present at the pre-transplant baseline in patients who subsequently developed rejection and remained detectable across the transplant course, indicating that it reflects recipient baseline immune biology rather than a consequence of graft injury. Longitudinal metabolomic profiling in this cohort identified time-dependent metabolic changes, including in amino acid metabolism that co-occur with the {gamma}{delta} signature and converge with it upon multi-omics integration. At the pre-transplant baseline, {gamma}{delta} T-cell marker expression alone showed exploratory discriminatory value for rejection risk (AUC = 0.69), improving marginally when integrated with metabolomic features (AUC = 0.71); larger prospective studies will be needed before clinical translation.
